summary: Proceed with no companion. This is a single-flag change on an untested call (w2), and its main effect lands at bs=1, where the per-shape median is tight (err about 0.5 us on 48.8 us), so a win or a loss of 1-2 us can be read. Two premises need fixing: keep use_fp32_reduce=True, and keep the cache13 aliasing so the self-check actually tests the zeroing.
justification: Mechanism: w2 has size_n = H = 4096 and size_k = I = 4096 with top_k=1. That gives half as many N tiles as w13 (8192) over the same K. At bs=1 under ep8 only about 1 local route is active, so Marlin's flattened (m-blocks x n-tiles x k-tiles) space over 528 resident CTAs (workspace 4 per SM) splits each n-tile's K across more slices than w13 does. The lock-ordered fp32 reduce chain is therefore deeper, and that chain is what atomic add collapses. This is plausible, and it is genuinely the untested half: w13-marlin-atomic-add-small-m changed only w13, on the old parity base. WEAKEST LINK: the strongest prior is against it. The w13 run's Marlin row at bs=1 was 44.4 us against the base's ~41-45, a true zero at the shape with the deepest slicing. vLLM/SGLang's dense heuristic (should_use_atomic_add_reduce) enables atomic add only for n < 2048 and k >= 2048. w2's n = 4096 is still outside that range, so the upstream authors' own measurements say global reduce wins at this n. Expected directions: faster at bs=1 is the only one with real support. At bs=8/16/32, slice_count is about 1-2, and at slice_count 1 the reduce is skipped entirely, so expect flat there, not faster. If a cache3.zero_() is needed, it costs a ~1-1.5 us memset at every gated shape (2 MB at bs=32), which can turn bs=8-32 slightly slower. Readability: the Marlin profile row aggregates both launches and moves about ±20% between runs of identical code (bs=16 read 114-176 us on the same code), so the brief's 'read the Marlin row' cannot attribute a few us. Judge on per-shape medians instead: decode_1's err is about 0.5 us, so a 1-2 us change there is z 2-4. Read the memset row for the zeroing cost. At the headline, a 3 us gain at bs=1 alone is about 1% geomean, inside the CI, so the per-shape median is the read.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity: it sets the shared workspace (max_blocks_per_sm=4 -> 528 CTAs), which sets slice_count and therefore the size of any atomic-add effect. This is fixed on master, so it does not confound this run, but a result here does not transfer to a different workspace.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: at bs<32 it consumes y (= cache3) via y.contiguous() and indexes by local_ids. Rows of remote routes are never written by Marlin in either mode, so atomic add changes nothing there. But if the implementer zeroes cache3, those rows become 0 instead of stale cache1 data. That is harmless only if the combine kernel masks remote slots, which it should already do, and the self-check confirms it.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack: its sorted_ids/n_padded padding (BSM 8 at bs<=16, 16 at bs=32) sets the m-block count and thus the slicing depth. It is unchanged here, so the comparison is clean, but a later block_size_m change at small M would shift this flag's value.
interference: No companion. The change is one flag on one call, plus at most one memset that has its own profile row. A gain at bs=1 is attributable to the w2 atomic reduce, and a flat or loss result retires the knob for both Marlin calls. A loss is unambiguous because the memset row says how much of it is the zeroing. An 'atomic on w13 and w2' stack is pointless while w13 alone measured zero. An ab-tune of the workspace (blocks per SM) would be informative, since deeper slicing means more for atomics to save, but it belongs in a follow-up only if this run gains at bs=1.
rules_flags: No rule break. The branch is on num_tokens only, the zero_() is a capturable memset on a preallocated view, and nothing is cached from data. bf16 atomic accumulation of k-slice partials is a Marlin option that SGLang/vLLM expose. It is not a stored-precision change, and the activations stay BF16.

Precision margin: each k-slice partial is rounded to bf16 before the atomic add, so at bs=1/4 (deepest slicing) w2's output carries maybe 0.3-0.8% extra relative error. The 1.5% bound should hold, but the per-row 5x bound on near-zero rows is the one to watch. The pre-timing tests at bs=1 and bs=4 exercise exactly this case. A self-check bound of 5e-3 against master is reasonable.
Atomic add makes outputs nondeterministic in the last bits. That is allowed, but the self-check must compare with a tolerance, never bit-exactly.
open_questions: Spec correction: do NOT set use_fp32_reduce=False. The w13 implementation established that the pair is not required: vLLM's MoE runner passes atomic add with use_fp32_reduce=True, and c_tmp is allocated only when fp32_reduce && !atomic. Keeping True also keeps this the same knob that w13 tested. Flip it only if the binding rejects the combination, and log the error text.

Is the zero_() needed? cache3 aliases cache13, which holds w13's output (cache1) at the time w2 runs, so the buffer is guaranteed non-zero. Keep that aliasing: it makes the prepare self-check a true test of whether Marlin's atomic path pre-zeroes (or plain-stores slice 0) or needs an explicit zero. Do not give cache3 a fresh buffer, because a freshly cudaMalloc'd buffer may read as zero and hide a missing zero_().
What is the actual slice_count for w2 at bs=1 (it depends on Marlin's thread_n/thread_k pick for m_block 8)? Printing it once from the bank shapes would show whether a 2-5 us win is even possible.
Does profile.txt list the two Marlin launches separately? If yes, read w2's own row. If not, rely on the per-shape median and treat the aggregated Marlin row as noise.
